source.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
source.text: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come to market. draft.threads_post:
Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that creates video feeds filled entirely with personalized, AI-generated videos and ads.

The system uses demographic data and viewing history to write prompts for an LLM, which then generates custom videos tailored to each user. Patent examiners rejected the filing, but Google could still appeal or submit an amended version.

Would you watch an AI video feed made just for you, or stick to human creators?

Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that creates video feeds filled entirely with personalized, AI-generated videos and ads.

According to patent documents spotted by Patentlyze, the system uses your demographic data and viewing history to automatically write prompts. Those prompts are fed into an LLM to generate custom videos tailored to what you watch.

The patent has been rejected for now, though Google could still appeal or resubmit an amended version.
